claims.title: Rise of the Nok culture
claims.summary: On the central Nigerian plateau the Nok culture emerged, producing distinctive terracotta sculpture and, in its later phases, smelting iron — among the earliest such traditions in sub-Saharan Africa.

sources.label: Nok Terracottas (Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History)
A Chronology of the Central Nigerian Nok Culture, 1500 BC to the Beginning of the Common Era
sources.publisher: Peter Breunig and Nicole Rupp (academic study)

claims.title: Nok terracottas first recognised
claims.summary: Terracotta heads unearthed near the village of Nok during tin-mining drew scholarly attention, giving the ancient culture its name and revealing the antiquity of Nigerian art.

sources.label: Nok Terracottas (Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History)

claims.title: The bronzes of Igbo-Ukwu
claims.summary: An Igbo community at Igbo-Ukwu produced sophisticated cast-bronze ritual objects and vast quantities of trade beads, evidence of advanced metalworking and long-distance trade in the southeastern forests.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-850-the-bronzes-of-igbo-ukwu, claim TL:NGA:event:850:the-bronzes-of-igbo-ukwu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Kanem empire
claims.summary: Around Lake Chad the empire of Kanem emerged under the Sayfawa dynasty, growing wealthy as the southern terminus of the trans-Saharan trade and gradually adopting Islam.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-800-rise-of-the-kanem-empire, claim TL:NGA:event:800:rise-of-the-kanem-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Shift from Kanem to Bornu
claims.summary: After conflict with the Bulala forced the dynasty to abandon its eastern heartland, the state re-centred west of Lake Chad at Bornu, beginning the era of the Bornu Empire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1400-shift-from-kanem-to-bornu, claim TL:NGA:event:1400:shift-from-kanem-to-bornu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peak of Bornu under Idris Alooma
claims.summary: Mai Idris Alooma reformed Bornu's army and administration, extended its control over central Saharan trade routes, and deepened the role of Islamic law at its height of power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1570-peak-of-bornu-under-idris-alooma, claim TL:NGA:event:1570:peak-of-bornu-under-idris-alooma, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Flourishing of Benin and Oyo
claims.summary: The Edo kingdom of Benin and the Yoruba empire of Oyo rose as major forest powers, Benin renowned for its court art and Oyo for the cavalry empire of its Alaafin.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1300-flourishing-of-benin-and-oyo, claim TL:NGA:event:1300:flourishing-of-benin-and-oyo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Atlantic slave trade
claims.summary: European demand drew the Bights of Benin and Biafra into the transatlantic slave trade; ports such as Bonny and Old Calabar became major export points, and vast numbers of people were deported in conditions of extreme violence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1500-the-atlantic-slave-trade, claim TL:NGA:event:1500:the-atlantic-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Usman dan Fodio launches his jihad
claims.summary: The Fulani scholar Usman dan Fodio began a jihad in the Hausa lands, rallying followers against the existing rulers and igniting a religious and political revolution across the north.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1804-usman-dan-fodio-launches-his-jihad, claim TL:NGA:event:1804:usman-dan-fodio-launches-his-jihad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Sokoto Caliphate
claims.summary: Dan Fodio's victories consolidated into the Sokoto Caliphate, a vast confederation of emirates under Islamic law that became one of nineteenth-century Africa's largest states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1808-founding-of-the-sokoto-caliphate, claim TL:NGA:event:1808:founding-of-the-sokoto-caliphate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain abolishes its slave trade
claims.summary: Britain outlawed its own transatlantic slave trade and began naval patrols of the West African coast, though illegal slaving from the region continued for decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1807-britain-abolishes-its-slave-trade, claim TL:NGA:event:1807:britain-abolishes-its-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain annexes Lagos
claims.summary: After occupying Lagos in 1851, Britain annexed it as a crown colony in 1861, establishing a coastal foothold from which colonial power spread into the interior.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Nigeria
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: British sack of Benin City
claims.summary: A British punitive expedition destroyed Benin City, exiled the Oba, and looted thousands of the Benin Bronzes, dispersing centuries of court art to foreign museums and collectors.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1897-british-sack-of-benin-city, claim TL:NGA:event:1897:british-sack-of-benin-city, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of the Sokoto Caliphate
claims.summary: Frederick Lugard's forces defeated the Sokoto army in March 1903; the last independent sultan, Attahiru I, was killed at Burmi in July, ending the caliphate's independence and bringing the north under British control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1903-fall-of-the-sokoto-caliphate, claim TL:NGA:event:1903:fall-of-the-sokoto-caliphate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Amalgamation of Nigeria
claims.summary: Lord Lugard joined the Northern and Southern Protectorates into a single Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria, creating the territorial shape of the modern country under indirect rule.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Nigeria
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Nigeria gains independence
claims.summary: Nigeria became an independent state within the Commonwealth on 1 October 1960, with Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa as its first prime minister; it became a republic in 1963.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Nigeria
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

sources.label: Nigeria gained independence from the United Kingdom

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1960-nigeria-gains-independence, claim TL:NGA:event:1960:nigeria-gains-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Military coups and unrest
claims.summary: A January 1966 coup killed Prime Minister Balewa; a July counter-coup and ensuing violence against Igbo communities deepened the crisis that would lead to civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1966-military-coups-and-unrest, claim TL:NGA:event:1966:military-coups-and-unrest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Secession of Biafra
claims.summary: Colonel Odumegwu Ojukwu declared the Eastern Region an independent Republic of Biafra, precipitating the Nigerian Civil War.

sources.label: Civil war breaks out in Nigeria (6 July 1967)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1967-secession-of-biafra, claim TL:NGA:event:1967:secession-of-biafra, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Nigerian Civil War
claims.summary: Federal forces under General Gowon fought to reunify the country and blockaded Biafra; the resulting famine and fighting killed an estimated one to two million people, mostly civilians, before Biafra surrendered in January 1970.

sources.label: Civil war breaks out in Nigeria (6 July 1967)

claims.title: Abuja chosen as new capital
claims.summary: Amid an oil-fuelled boom, the federal government decided to build a new, centrally located capital at Abuja to replace Lagos, a project realised over the following decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1976-abuja-chosen-as-new-capital, claim TL:NGA:event:1976:abuja-chosen-as-new-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annulled election and Abacha's rule
claims.summary: The military annulled the 1993 presidential election, widely believed won by Moshood Abiola, ushering in the repressive regime of General Sani Abacha until his death in 1998.

sources.label: Abacha, Abiola, and Nigeria's 1999 Transition to Civilian Rule

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-1993-annulled-election-and-abacha-s-rule, claim TL:NGA:event:1993:annulled-election-and-abacha-s-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to civilian rule and the Fourth Republic
claims.summary: The military handed power to the elected president Olusegun Obasanjo, ending sixteen years of military government and inaugurating the Fourth Republic, Nigeria's longest period of continuous civilian rule.

sources.label: Abacha, Abiola, and Nigeria's 1999 Transition to Civilian Rule

claims.title: Africa's largest economy
claims.summary: After rebasing its GDP, Nigeria was confirmed as the largest economy in Africa, underscoring its weight as the continent's most populous nation and a major oil producer.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nigeria: From the Nok artisans and the great Sahelian and forest kingdoms to a colonial amalgamation, a hard-won independence, and Africa's most populous nation.", terralore.co/country/NGA/chronicle#ev-2014-africa-s-largest-economy, claim TL:NGA:event:2014:africa-s-largest-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First opposition election victory
claims.summary: Muhammadu Buhari defeated the sitting president Goodluck Jonathan, the first time an opposition candidate won Nigeria's presidency through the ballot box, marking a democratic milestone.

sources.label: Assessing Twenty-Five Years of Democracy in Nigeria
